lines.trans: Mr. Muranishi, watch over our shoot again today.
Hey, this video is going to sell for sure.
Wait—what do you think you are doing?!
I said you can't have that!
Damn you, what the hell do you think you're doing?!
Were you planning to sell this on the black market?

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Special reading きょう.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Core adverb in set greetings like よろしくお願いします and どうぞよろしく.
With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Meaning: Mitamura.

examples.text: 三田村ちゃんと豚足食え

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。
お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。

meanings.note: Opposite of 表 (public surface); 裏の世界 means 'the underworld / hidden world'.

examples.text: 裏の世界を見せてやろうか。
examples.trans: Shall I show you the hidden world?
Write on the back of the paper.

examples.text: 古谷さんと手組んで、うちの作品を裏で流す。
examples.trans: Team up with Furuya and distribute our films underground.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
